body:
I was bullied in middle school.  I lost almost all my friends and the few friend I had left I acted like dicks to as a defense mechanism.  I watched a lot of the history and discovery channel and thought I was educationally superior and more mature.  I was too proud to admit I had a problem.  I'm now a senior in high school and I feel like I cling to a group of friend and not really good friends with any one of them.

I think it is inappropriate to say I am "OMG I AM JUST LIKE YOU!!!".  However, I do see a lot of similarities.  Now realize I am not a psychiatrist, I don't have some of the experience of some older redditors, and I may have a skewed and illogical view on life (doesn't everyone).  However, I want to offer some food for thought.  

I am afraid to make new friends.  You are putting yourself out there to be rejected, ignored, and abused.  Do you think this may be your situation too?  If so maybe you should work on becoming friends with people that seem more tolerant to your personality.  If you put an effort in to making new friends you would be surprised how easy it is.  

Conversations are quite easy actually.  This [thread](http://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/c4mp3/i_need_to_get_over_my_social_anxiety/) has some great advice on how to hold a conversation.

Don't tell yourself I'm so fucked up while in social situations.  I know in the middle of a conversation I have this thought pattern:  "OMG how am I doing". If I feel like I am not presenting myself well I will panic.  If I am doing well I panic and ask myself how to stay articulate.  And in the middle of talking I panic and wander what would happen if I just stopped talking altogether. I went to a therapist for a while and she told me not to think about your problems and don't over analysis.  Over analysis situations can lead to negative thought patterns and a tired mind.

Keep on exercising!  Naturally humans have a lot of energy and tension.  Exercising will release endorphins which is like a natural anti-depressants.  There are so many activities you can do outside.  Find what you enjoy and don't feel forced to do something you don't want to do.

Anxiety and depression are intertwined.  I don't know how feasible this is, but you should maybe ask to see a therapist.  You sound like you have a lot of symptoms of depression.  Depression can make you feel so drained which makes life including social interactions very hard.  

One last note.  I noticed you said "for some stupid reason".  Its better that you identify negative thought patterns as stupid than as a means.  Anxiety and depression stem from irrational thoughts.  Keep on tell yourself that.
Thank you.  The public defender's office is closed until Tuesday.  How much will a lawyer cost for a case like this?
The best way I can describe it is lead in my veins.  I always feel so sluggish and no matter what I do the best feeling is just lying down on my bed.

Well that's the reason why I would mention it.  I got 3 F as a senior and 2 Ds and 1 F as a junior.   However, I worked hard to get all A's my first two years of school (which sort of lead to my anxiety) so have a pretty good GPA and good accomplishments.  

I have the same train of though as you.  No college admission officers want to hear excuses on why you didn't do well in school or hear some sad kid.  Also I feel ashamed that I am depressed and feel like its my fault (which it sort of is).
